item.title: Technology and apps
item.description: Everyday words for phones, apps, accounts and staying safe online.

children.definition: money you pay regularly, often every month, to use a service
children.example: I cancelled my music subscription because I rarely used it.

children.definition: to move your finger quickly across a touch screen
children.example: Swipe left to see the next photo.

children.definition: to enter your name and password so you can use an account
children.example: I can't log in because I forgot my password.

children.definition: a short number sent to your phone to prove it is really you
children.example: Never tell anyone the verification code from your bank.

children.definition: a short message an app shows on your screen to tell you about something
children.example: I turn off notifications when I'm studying.

children.definition: a program you use to look at websites on the internet
children.example: Try opening the page in a different browser.

children.definition: the space on a device for keeping photos, files and apps
children.example: I can't take more photos because my storage is full.

children.definition: a picture of what is on your screen at one moment
children.example: Send me a screenshot of the error message.

children.definition: (of a program) to stop working suddenly
children.example: The game crashes every time I open the map.

children.definition: the part of a phone or app where you choose how it works
children.example: You can change the language in the settings.

children.definition: the right to keep your personal information to yourself
children.example: Check who can see your photos in the privacy options.

children.definition: a dishonest plan to trick people and take their money
children.example: A message saying you've won a prize is usually a scam.
